label: COMMERCIAL PROPOSAL / DESIGN REFERENCE
title: A clear plan for your site
subtitle: A reusable proposal structure for energy and connected infrastructure. Replace this explanatory content with verified project inputs.

sections.title: The decision
paragraphs: Lead with the decision the customer needs to make. Explain the site need, the proposed scope and the expected practical benefit in plain language. Keep the opening useful to a reader who has not attended the sales meeting.

rows: Document existing conditions, customer priorities and available evidence.
Define the engineering scope, required approvals and responsibility for each dependency.
Identify included equipment and work, sequencing and commissioning requirements.
Describe documentation, training and agreed service responsibilities.

sections.title: Commercial clarity
paragraphs: Present verified pricing, payment milestones, schedule dependencies and exclusions together. Make scope boundaries easy to find. Keep internal margins and supplier negotiations out of the customer document.
sections.note: This is a design specimen, not a project quotation. No prices, savings, warranties or delivery dates are asserted.

sections.title: Terms that support a decision
paragraphs: A proposal should explain what happens next, who owns each step and which conditions must be satisfied before delivery begins. Use a table when those responsibilities are easier to compare side by side.

rows: Agreed inclusions, exclusions and acceptance criteria

items.title: Site conditions
items.text: State the evidence used and any conditions that still need inspection. Avoid language implying that unknown conditions have already been resolved.

items.title: Schedule dependencies
items.text: Separate target dates from contractual commitments. Identify utility, permitting, procurement and customer dependencies when relevant.

items.title: Performance and support
items.text: Use the actual agreed terms and manufacturer documentation. Do not import guarantees from an older proposal or website.

sections.title: Next step
paragraphs: Close with one specific customer action and the documents needed to support it. Keep the call to action practical and consistent with the proposal's current status.
